==History==
The origin of its foundation is unknown. Many people of {{ill|Nakatomi clan|ar|ناكاتومي|de|Nakatomi (Klan)|es|Clan Nakatomi|fa|خاندان ناکاتومی|fr|Clan Nakatomi|it|Clan Nakatomi|ja|中臣氏|ko|나카토미씨|nl|Nakatomi-clan|pl|Nakatomi (ród)|pt|Clã Nakatomi|vi|Gia tộc Nakatomi|zh|中臣氏|qid=Q1198447}} origin lived in this area, came to call themselves the Sugo clan from the place name, and ruled the region as local magnates. It is considered that this Sugo clan enshrined their {{ill|Oyagami|fr|Oyagami|it|Oyagami|ja|祖神|simple|Oyagami|qid=Q85882782}} Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto as their {{ill|Ujigami|de|Ujigami|es|Ujigami|fa|اوجی‌گامی|fr|Ujigami|ja|氏神|ko|씨신|mni|ꯎꯖꯤꯒꯃꯤ|pl|Ujigami|ro|Ujigami|simple|Ujigami|te|ఉజిగామి|uk|Удзіґамі|zh|氏神|qid=Q767655}}. The earliest documentary appearance is in ''Shinshō Kakuchokufu'', which says: “In {{ill|Empress Kōken|ar|الإمبراطورة شوتوكو|azb|امپراتریس کوکن|bcl|Emperatris Kōken|be|Імператрыца ranked as a major shrine.

In the medieval period, when {{ill|Tenjin faith|ja|天神信仰|ko|천신신앙|qid=Q66890725}} spread, shrine monks of this shrine’s {{ill|Jingū-ji|fr|Jingū-ji|it|Jingū-ji|ja|神宮寺|pl|Jingū-ji|ru|Дзингудзи|zh|神宮寺|qid=Q1074971}} (Kōmatsu-zan Tenmon-ji) promoted a tradition that “Sugakō was born at the edge of Sugasawa in the precincts,” invited Tenjin, and enshrined him together. Sugasawa still exists in the precincts today. In time it came to be called “Sugo Tenmangū,” and in the Edo period Tenjin came to be treated as the main deity.
